messages:
sam: FYI customer reported intermittent failing streams to their private inference endpoint in VPC, symptoms: TLS handshake timeouts and occasional 502s. Happening since yesterday afternoon.
maria: which customer / endpoint? any repro steps yet?
sam: corp-acme, endpoint vpce-0123 in us-east-1. They see curl failures from their on-prem NAT box: `curl -v https://10.0.5.7:443` -> `* SSL_connect: connection reset by peer` then timeout.
lee: can we see tcpdump from inside the VPC node and from the NAT? want to confirm return port behavior.
sam: customer provided tcpdump from their NAT egress showing lots of SYN->SYN/ACK then RST from our side. snippet: 
```
10:12:01.123456 IP 198.51.100.22.52345 > 10.0.5.7.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,...]
10:12:01.123524 IP 10.0.5.7.443 > 198.51.100.22.52345: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960
10:12:01.124001 IP 10.0.5.7.443 > 198.51.100.22.52345: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0
```
We see server ACK then immediate RST.
irene: that pattern often indicates stateless NACL rejecting return traffic because ephemeral return port doesn't match allowlist. what do the customer NACL rules show?
sam: customer pasted NACL egress rules: allow 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443 (rule 100), DENY 0.0.0.0/0 ALL (rule 200). inbound rules only allow 10.0.0.0/16 -> TCP 443 (rule 100) then deny all.
network-eng: wait, NACLs are stateless so you need to allow ephemeral ports on both inbound and outbound depending on traffic direction. If their on-prem initiates to our VPC endpoint, the return packets use ephemeral ports on the on-prem side — the ephemeral port range must be allowed by the NACL.
maria: what ephemeral range are they allowing?
sam: looks like they only allowed 1024-65535 UDP (weird) but TCP ephemeral range isn't explicitly allowed. their ACLs were created by a template that only focused on UDP.
lee: can reproduce quickly — please ask customer to run `sudo tcpdump -n -i <nat-if> tcp and host 10.0.5.7` while we attempt a curl from their NAT and collect full pcap. Also ask them to run `curl --connect-timeout 10 -v https://10.0.5.7:443 --tlsv1.2` and paste client-side logs.
sam: already have curl logs: `* Connected to 10.0.5.7 (10.0.5.7) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.0.5.7:443
* Closing connection 0`
irene: suggests TCP tear before TLS completes. fix is to add explicit ephemeral port allowance in the NACL: add egress allow rule for TCP ports 1024-65535 to 198.51.100.0/24 (their on-prem) and similarly inbound allow for ephemeral from that CIDR to the endpoint. Also ensure rule numbers are ordered before any broader deny.
network-eng: note AWS NACL evaluation is by rule number ascending; deny-all at 200 will block if allow rule numbers are higher. Their allow rule 100 for port 443 is fine, but ephemeral allow must be numbered <200, e.g., 150.
lee: another angle — if they have a security group that restricts source ports (rare), confirm SGs don't have source port constraints. SGs are stateful so usually OK.
maria: can we craft a minimal repro command for them?
sam: yes: from their NAT device run: `# start dump on NAT`
`sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.0.5.7 and tcp port 443 -w /tmp/curl.pcap`
`# in another shell`
`curl -v https://10.0.5.7:443 --connect-timeout 10`
Send pcap to us. Also ask them to temporarily add a NACL egress allow TCP 1024-65535 to their NAT CIDR and retest.
irene: include a safe rollback note for them: add rule number 150 allow TCP 1024-65535 to their NAT CIDR, test, then remove if not needed.
network-eng: added: also watch for ALB / target group idle timeouts — if they have long-lived streams our infra might hit keepalive settings. but current logs point to immediate RST so fix NACL first.
sam: I'll send step-by-step to customer and cc network-eng to watch their account while they flip NACL. will follow up with results. thanks. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deploy alert: made a note on ticket INC-4582 for follow-up in 24h.
maria: thanks — if they still see resets after ephemeral rules, we'll ask for VPC flow logs + full pcap and escalate to infra oncall.
